{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mo-f","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"48b9875b3bac076f9a477160df6724382a0b8e4f40631a6c7e51071f852b3463","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mo-class-f:lineage:64","source_registry_sha256":"f128002157e581eb7004b9370c8cfbafd7b29a1596262980704fbda0a45932f5","source_liveness_sha256":"fdf72d02e75b9589fee5aaf5b83ec9705ff03586f574464e3553a827f9b698d8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Missouri mandatory insurance: liability insurance and proof, other forms of financial responsibility, minimum coverage, keeping insurance, suspensions for lapses and unpaid damages, what to do after a crash, the Move It law, and accident reports","heading":"C — Mandatory insurance: financial responsibility, accepted proof, self-insurance and bonds, minimum and uninsured motorist coverage, keeping proof in the vehicle, lapse and unpaid-damage suspensions, crash steps, steer it and clear it, and filing an accident report","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Mandatory insurance: financial responsibility, accepted proof, self-insurance and bonds, minimum and uninsured motorist coverage, keeping proof in the vehicle, lapse and unpaid-damage suspensions, crash steps, steer it and clear it, and filing an accident report
Knowledge domain: why Missouri requires liability insurance, which documents prove it, the other ways to show financial responsibility, the minimum coverage amounts, the duty to keep insurance and carry proof, what happens when insurance lapses or crash damages go unpaid, the steps to take after a crash, the law on moving vehicles after minor crashes, and when an accident report must be filed.

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
State law requires every motor vehicle operator and owner to carry some form of liability insurance, which is called Financial Responsibility. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Liability insurance covers the policyholder's legal liability when other people are injured or their property is damaged. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Vehicle owners must show proof of insurance when they register a vehicle or renew their plates. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Accepted proof includes a copy of your current insurance ID card, your policy or a binder, a paid receipt showing the policy, a Department self-insurance certificate or bond ID card, or a handheld electronic device. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
A binder is a temporary insurance policy. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
To be self-insured you must have more than 25 vehicles and show that you can and will pay for damage they cause, and the Department then issues a certificate of self-insurance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
Insuring through a surety bond, certificate of deposit or other negotiable securities means filing $75,000, or $150,000 for a real estate bond, with the Department. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
Another option is depositing $75,000 in cash with the State Treasurer, after which the Department issues a certificate of self-insurance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
The minimum liability coverage is $25,000 per person for bodily injury. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
The minimum liability coverage is $50,000 per crash for bodily injury. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
The minimum liability coverage is $25,000 per crash for property damage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A01
You must also carry uninsured motorist coverage of $25,000 per person and $50,000 per crash for bodily injury. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A02
When you register a vehicle, you sign a form saying you have insurance and will keep it on the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A02
Keep proof of insurance in your vehicle, because you will be ticketed if an officer asks for it and you cannot show it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A02
The Department may ask for proof of insurance at any time, and it will require proof if you were in a crash and did not show it then. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A02
Letting your insurance lapse can cost a great deal of money after a crash and can lead to losing your driver license and license plates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A02
If the Department finds out you have not kept insurance, it mails you a notice of suspension, and your license and plates may be taken or suspended. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A02
Proof of insurance is most often filed as an SR-22, which your insurance company or agent files for you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
If you fail to keep insurance for the required three years, your license and/or plates are suspended again. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A02
A driver who causes an accident and leaves the resulting damages unpaid has the license and/or plates suspended for one year. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A02
You can be reinstated within that one year by paying a $20 fee and sending the Driver License Bureau proof that the damages were settled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A02
After one insurance suspension, your license and/or plates stay suspended until you pay a $20 fee and file proof of insurance, which you must keep doing for three years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A02
Two suspensions within two years of each other bring a 90-day suspension, a $200 fee, and three years of proof of insurance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A02
Three or more suspensions bring a one-year suspension, a $400 fee, and three years of proof of insurance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A03
A traffic crash is any time you injure yourself or someone else or damage property while driving your vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A03
Do not leave even after hitting a parked vehicle, because leaving the scene of a traffic crash is a crime. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A03
After a crash, stop, and move your vehicle off the road if you can, especially if it could cause more crashes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F28 | anchor: A03
Help anyone who is hurt and keep them comfortable without moving them, then call an ambulance and the police. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F29 | anchor: A03
If the crash happens at night or in bad weather, warn other traffic with flares, reflectors or flashlights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F30 | anchor: A03
Exchange names, addresses, driver license numbers, VINs, plate numbers, and insurance companies and policy numbers with everyone involved. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F31 | anchor: A03
Stay at the scene until a law enforcement officer says you may leave, and contact your insurance company soon even if the crash was not your fault. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F32 | anchor: A03
Missouri law requires vehicles in minor crashes with no injuries to move off the road, onto the shoulder or another nearby spot. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F33 | anchor: A03
Each minute a stopped vehicle blocks one freeway lane backs up approaching traffic for four minutes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F34 | anchor: A03
Secondary crashes cause 18 percent of fatalities in Missouri, and the Move It law helps cut that risk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F35 | anchor: A03
When an accident report is required, state law says it must be filed within 30 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F36 | anchor: A03
A required report applies even to a parking lot accident or one already settled, if it happened in Missouri less than one year ago. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-F37 | anchor: A04
The report is required when someone involved had no liability insurance and there was property damage over $500 or any injury or death. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec15-F38 | anchor: A04
You may get a Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Form 1140, from the Department's website, your insurer or agent, or any license office, and mail or fax it in. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec15-F39 | anchor: A04
Hitting a highway worker or emergency responder inside a designated construction, work or emergency zone can lead to revocation of your driving privilege. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

Misconceptions: a crash with a parked vehicle is still a crash you must not leave; after a minor crash with no injuries you move the vehicle, but you never move an injured person; you contact your insurer even when the crash was not your fault; proof of insurance belongs in the vehicle, not at home.
Mnemonics: steer it and clear it for minor crashes; the coverage pattern reads twenty-five, fifty, twenty-five in thousands of dollars.
Glossary: liability insurance means coverage for harm you cause to other people or their property; Financial Responsibility means the legal duty to be able to pay for that harm; binder means a temporary insurance policy; SR filing means the insurer's proof-of-insurance filing with the state; uninsured motorist coverage means coverage for your injuries when the at-fault driver has no insurance; VIN means vehicle identification number.
Dynamic facts: coverage minimums, bond amounts, suspension fees and the accident report form number are statutory or administrative and can change, and the Move It campaign wording is dated to the guide's edition.
